subject: Emotions
title: Magic and Misdirection
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Magic and Misdirection.

hook.text: A magician shows you both hands empty, then pulls a coin from your ear. Your brain just failed a prediction.

buildup.text: Magicians don't break physics. They break your attention model. Misdirection exploits how prediction works.

discovery.text: Scientists study magic to understand attention. Change blindness means you miss obvious changes you're not tracking.

twist.text: The gorilla experiment proved this: people counting basketball passes missed a person in a gorilla suit walking through.

climax.text: Magic works because the brain can't process everything. It predicts, and magicians hack the predictions.

punchline.text: Magic isn't about tricking your eyes. It's about tricking your predictions.

quiz.question: What does the gorilla experiment demonstrate?
